steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to look for halves in everyday things around us! Food, objects, nature — halves are everywhere! Ready to go on a halves hunt?
steps.studentText: Today we look for halves (1/2) in everyday objects around us!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with everyday objects: chapati, orange, paper, cake — all cut in half
media.fallbackText: Owl teacher waving hello with everyday objects: chapati, orange, paper, cake — all cut in half

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn
steps.studentText: Today you will learn to find halves in everyday objects. A half means one of two equal parts. You will see halves in food, paper, and things around you!

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about halves in real life
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: Can you think of something at home that you can cut or fold into two equal parts? What would each part be called?
steps.studentText: What things at home can you cut or fold into two equal parts? What is each part called?

media.altText: A home scene with various objects: chapati, paper, fruit, cloth — with question marks
media.fallbackText: A home scene with various objects: chapati, paper, fruit, cloth — with question marks

interaction.question: Name something at home that you can divide into two equal parts. What would each part be called?
interaction.placeholder: I can cut/fold... into two equal parts. Each part is...

steps.title: Learn It
steps.purpose: Teach identifying halves in everyday objects
steps.owlText: Let me show you. When you cut a chapati into two equal pieces, each piece is one half of the chapati. When you fold a paper into two equal parts, each part is one half. When you cut an orange into two equal halves, each half is one half of the orange. The key is: the two parts must be equal — the same size!
steps.studentText: A half in real life: Cut or fold something into two equal parts. Each part is one half. The parts must be the same size!

media.altText: Three examples: (1) chapati cut into 2 equal pieces, (2) paper folded into 2 equal parts, (3) orange cut into 2 equal halves. Each labeled '1/2'.
media.caption: Halves in everyday objects: chapati, paper, orange.
media.fallbackText: Three examples: (1) chapati cut into 2 equal pieces, (2) paper folded into 2 equal parts, (3) orange cut into 2 equal halves. Each labeled '1/2'.

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect halves to many real-life contexts
steps.owlText: We see halves everywhere! A chapati cut in half. A piece of paper folded in half. An orange cut into two equal halves. A ribbon cut into two equal pieces. Even a door — each side is one half of the door! Halves are all around us!
steps.studentText: Halves are everywhere: food, paper, fruit, ribbons, doors. Look for things divided into two equal parts!

media.altText: Collage of everyday objects showing halves: chapati, paper, orange, ribbon, door
media.fallbackText: Collage of everyday objects showing halves: chapati, paper, orange, ribbon, door

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show worked examples of identifying halves in objects
steps.owlText: Let me show you how to spot halves. This chapati is cut into two equal pieces. Each piece is one half. How do I know? The two pieces are the same size! This paper is folded into two equal parts. Each part is one half. The parts match exactly — that is how you know they are equal.
steps.studentText: To spot halves: Look for two parts that are the same size. If both parts match exactly, each one is one half.

media.altText: Two examples: (1) chapati cut into 2 equal pieces with '1/2' label on each, (2) paper folded into 2 equal parts with matching edges shown.
media.fallbackText: Two examples: (1) chapati cut into 2 equal pieces with '1/2' label on each, (2) paper folded into 2 equal parts with matching edges shown.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.purpose: Practice identifying which object shows halves
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at these two objects. One object is divided into two equal parts. The other is not. Which object shows halves? Tap the correct one.
steps.studentText: Which object shows halves? Look for two equal parts.

media.altText: Two objects: (A) a chapati cut into 2 equal pieces, (B) a chapati cut into 2 unequal pieces.
media.fallbackText: Two objects: (A) a chapati cut into 2 equal pieces, (B) a chapati cut into 2 unequal pieces.

interaction.question: Which object shows halves?
options: Object A: chapati cut into 2 equal pieces
Object B: chapati cut into 2 unequal pieces
interaction.correctAnswer: Object A: chapati cut into 2 equal pieces
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! Object A has two equal pieces. Each piece is one half. The parts are the same size!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Look for the object where both parts are the same size. That is what makes halves — equal parts!

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.purpose: Test understanding of halves in real objects (QC-H2)
steps.owlText: Quick check! A chapati is cut into 2 equal pieces. You get 1 piece. What fraction of the chapati do you have?
steps.studentText: A chapati is cut into 2 equal pieces. You get 1 piece. What fraction of the chapati do you have?

media.altText: A chapati cut into 2 equal pieces. One piece is highlighted for the child.
media.fallbackText: A chapati cut into 2 equal pieces. One piece is highlighted for the child.

interaction.question: A chapati is cut into 2 equal pieces. You get 1 piece. What fraction do you have?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Correct! One piece out of 2 equal pieces is one half. Good thinking!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: The chapati was cut into 2 equal pieces. You have 1 of those pieces. That is one half.

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. Where can you find halves in everyday life? What does 'equal parts' mean? You are a halves detective!
steps.studentText: What did you learn about finding halves in everyday objects?

interaction.question: How do you feel about finding halves in everyday objects?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You learned to find halves in everyday objects today. Look around you — halves are in your food, your paper, your world! Keep being a halves detective!
steps.studentText: You learned to find halves in everyday objects! Look for halves everywhere!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I found halves!'
media.fallbackText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I found halves!'
